[[Rhosymedre]], [[Wrexham]] | capacity = 3,000 (500 seated) | chairman = Des Williams | manager = Ryan Roberts | league = {{Welsh football updater|CefnDru}} | season = {{Welsh football updater|CefnDru2}} | position = {{Welsh football updater|CefnDru3}} | pattern_la1 = _redborder | pattern_b1 = _blackstripes | pattern_ra1 = _redborder | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = FFFFFF | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = 000000 | pattern_la2 = | pattern_b2 = _thingoldsides2 | pattern_ra2 = | leftarm2 = FF0000 | body2 = FF0000 | rightarm2 = FF0000 | shorts2 = FF0000 | socks2 = FF0000 | website = https://www.cefndruidsafc.com/ }} '''Cefn Druids Association Football Club''' ({{langx|cy|Clwb Pêl-droed Derwyddon Cefn}}) is a [[association football|football]] team based in the village of [[Cefn Mawr]], [[Wrexham (county borough)|Wrexham]]. The club was founded in 1872 by [[Llewelyn Kenrick]] who would later go on to found the [[Football Association of Wales]]. Following several mergers through the club's history, in 1992 it became Cefn Druids AFC with the amalgamation of Cefn Albion F.C. and [[Druids United F.C.|Druids United]]. The club is one of the oldest and most successful in Wales, winning the [[Welsh Cup]] 8 times and competing in 14 finals, most recently in 2012. The club has seen a resurgence in recent times with a successful run in the top flight, securing their best ever league finish and winning the European Play-Off, taking them into the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] for the second time. In [[2021–22 Cymru Premier|2021–22]], the club played in the [[Cymru North]] after being relegated from the [[Cymru Premier]] but withdrew ahead of the 2023–24 season due to the management and playing staff leaving over unpaid wages and a transfer ban by FIFA.{{cite news |title=Cefn Druids withdraw from Cymru North for 2023-24 season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65966366 |access-date=20 June 2023 |work=BBC Sport |date=20 June 2023 |archive-date=20 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620174744/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65966366 |url-status=live }} The club reformed in the 2024–25 season to play in the [[North East Wales Football League]] Championship Division.{{cite news |title=Bellevue clash lined up as Cefn Druids are back in action |url=https://www.leaderlive.co.uk/sport/24521040.bellevue-clash-lined-cefn-druids-back-action/ |access-date=19 August 2024 |work=Leaderlive |date=16 August 2024 }} They currently play in the {{Welsh football updater|CefnDru}}. The team's first choice strip is black and white striped shirts, black shorts and black socks. The second choice strip is red shirts, red shorts and red socks for the 2019–20 season. The club's official kit is produced by Italian kit giant [[Erreà|Errea]] with sponsorship by [[Wrexham Lager Brewery|Wrexham Lager]] and Johnstown Tyre Service."}}
